title: HTTP and Javalin
description: Serving data over HTTP: how a request travels from browser to server, HTTP methods, status codes and JSON, routes and handlers in Javalin, and lambdas as handlers, then the F16 project briefs: an in-memory repository behind an interface, wiring routes, service and repository end to end, and error responses.
sourceCoverageNotes: Course slice: Foundation days F4-F18 (curriculum/snapshot/pep-curriculum.json /tracks/0/weeks/0/days/3 to /tracks/0/weeks/3/days/2). This module covers F15, F16 (/tracks/0/weeks/2/days/4, /tracks/0/weeks/3/days/0).
Module grouping is a second-mate grouping decision recorded at intake (matrix record source-gap-java-foundations-modules), not syllabus: modules follow calendar day order and hold 4-9 topics.
Every calendar row of these days maps to exactly one topic with relation exact; there are no splits or shared rows.

F16 is a Project day: each of its three rows is one reusable learner-facing project brief (kind lab-brief, because the topic schema has no project kind) with a topic coding lab holding the starter scaffold and public tests, test command mvn -q -o test (captain decision pep-project-rows, option A; intake reconciliation education-01 and java-sme-001). The same canonical brief is reused by the Standard and Fast overlays.
